A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RACTD research work, with all 18 pages and Appendices A–H available. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable assessment of the text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original RACTD evaluations on Gym-MuJoCo, FrankaKitchen and Maze2d, inference timings, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, inference measurements and ablations, including the main-text and appendix results.

M1.justification: The teacher–student architecture, frozen reward model, combined CTM/DSM/reward objective and inference procedures in Section 3 and the appendices are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gym-MuJoCo, FrankaKitchen and Maze2d tasks, including the additional random/expert hopper datasets and kitchen-complete evaluation in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including Diffuser, Diffusion QL, Consistency AC/BC, Flow Q-learning and the sampling baselines.

E3.justification: The online/offline model-selection rules, planning horizons, open/closed-loop evaluation procedures, model sizes, sampling settings and metrics remain identical.

E4.justification: Figure 3's mode-selection analysis, Section 5's reward-placement ablation and Appendix E's loss-weight, sampling-step and observation/planning-horizon studies are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report RACTD means and standard errors over 100 planning seeds. Appendix E.3 retains its uncertainty reporting across 20 rollouts from intermediate checkpoints.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and empirical curves match. Examples include RACTD's MuJoCo averages of 96.4 offline and 101.5 online in Table 1, and its Maze2d average of 133.4 in Table 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–9 and Appendix G's proof sketch connecting reward-aware distillation to off-policy deterministic policy gradients are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: reward-aware single-step distillation, decoupled training, 9.7% improvement over prior methods and up to 142-fold inference speedup.

C2.justification: The mode-selection explanation, sample-diversity tradeoff, generalization discussion and limitations concerning three-network training, training instability and non-differentiable rewards remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, loss weights, noise schedules and hardware disclosures are identical. Both versions retain the same promise to release code upon acceptance, without new access information.

R1.justification: Section 6, the reference list and the paper's positioning relative to diffusion planners, consistency policies and actor-critic methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All substantive prose and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged by approximately 11% to fill the text width, shifting its caption downward. Its diagram content and caption wording are unchanged; all other figures, tables and body layout match.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication metadata and modestly enlarges Figure 1, providing a small readability adjustment. The scientific argument, experimental evidence, theory, limitations and reproducibility information are identical, so these presentation edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
